v.why: With a strong direct conv path already present, improving edge 0 has diminishing returns.
Redundant strong convs into the output give diminishing returns for a further conv upgrade.
A strong parent on edge 5 already supplies capacity to the output, so the gain from edge 3 shrinks.
A strong direct conv path buffers the loss from removing edge 5, making the edit less harmful.
With a strong direct path on edge 3, cutting edge 0 hurts less because the network does not rely on the intermediate nodes.
Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv restores a path and gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
A skip replacing a missing direct edge improves gradient flow, more than when replacing an existing op.
A skip that connects a previously disconnected intermediate path gains more than a swap.
Degrading a conv to pooling loses more than degrading a weak op.
Replacing none with a conv adds a new path, which gains more than replacing a pool or skip.
